title: The rack empties
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wednesday. Wood stops at the laundromat on the way home. The rack is empty. Forty copies. He stands there. The owner says a church group came through.

panels.composition: The laundromat, afternoon. The rack by the door: empty. WOOD in front of it with his hands in his coat.

image.prompt: a young man standing before an empty wire flyer rack in a laundromat, hands in his coat pockets, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The real-estate flyer still there. The church bulletin still there. The digest's slot empty.

image.prompt: close on a wire rack holding a real-estate flyer and a church bulletin with one slot empty, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The LAUNDRY owner at the dryers.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner unloading a dryer, speaking over her shoulder, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood at the door, looking at the rack. The strip has readers in Waldport who don't know it. He doesn't draw them. He can't.

image.prompt: a young man standing in a laundromat doorway looking back at an empty flyer rack, dryers turning, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Forty, to a church bus. Readers he'll never draw.
